summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and a tracheostomy was admitted from his nursing facility after an episode of coffee ground emesis. Initial evaluation showed leukocytosis with a white blood cell count of 25.5, which resolved within 12 hours. A CT scan revealed fluid-filled loops of bowel suggestive of mild enterocolitis, but no evidence of gastrointestinal bleeding. His elevated white count was likely reactive to urinary retention, with over one liter of urine drained via straight catheterization. He has chronic right leg pain, and imaging confirmed bilateral avascular necrosis of the femoral heads with early collapse on the right, as well as possible osteonecrosis in the right medial femoral condyle. Orthopedics recommended conservative management with a walker and follow-up in four weeks. He continued IV cefepime and oral linezolid for a recent multidrug-resistant UTI, with no growth on repeat urine culture. Oral vancomycin was continued to prevent C. diff recurrence during antibiotic treatment. He remained stable, afebrile, and without respiratory distress, and was discharged back to extended care with plans to complete antibiotics and follow up on urologic, orthopedic, and psychiatric management.
